question: What is the mass number of nitrogen?
solution:
The correct answer is **__14.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

**Nitrogen: **

__
 
• **Nitrogen** is a chemical element with the** symbol N, atomic number 7 and mass number 14.**
 
• Nitrogen is a **non-metal **and the **lightest element **in **group 15 **of the periodic table, also referred to as **pnictogens**.
 
• It is a **common element **in the universe and is thought to rank ninth in terms of overall abundance in both the Milky Way and the Solar System.
 
• At standard pressure and temperature, two of the element's atoms combine to form N₂, a **colourless **and **odourless diatomic gas**.
 
• N₂ is the most common **uncombined element **and makes up most of the Earth's atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

**Mass Number: **

 
• The total number of **protons **and **neutrons **in an atom's nucleus is known as the **mass number.**
 
• For instance, **uranium-235 **and **uranium-238** are the names of the two most well-known isotopes of uranium, those having mass numbers 235 and 238, respectively.
 
• Each **isotope **of an element is represented by the same literal symbol and has the same atomic number (number of protons).
